summary: Kiribati waives visas for citizens of around 120 countries and territories listed in its 2023 visa exemption order — including the UK, Ireland, most of the EU, the US, China, Japan, Australia, New Zealand and its Pacific neighbors — who may stay up to 90 days in any 12 months. Everyone else must obtain a visitor visa from Kiribati Immigration before traveling. All visitors need a passport valid six months, an onward ticket and funds for the stay.

declarations.text: Passengers complete a paper arrival card with customs and quarantine declarations, distributed on the flight. Food, plant material and animal products are controlled to protect a fragile atoll environment. Declare anything of the sort.

notes: The UK government says there is a strict quarantine regime for importing food, plant and animal (including fish) products.
Canada's travel advice says importing firearms, ammunition, explosives, counterfeit money and goods, knives and pornography is strictly prohibited.

payments.text: The UK government says very few places in Kiribati accept credit cards, and that there are ATMs at Bank of Kiribati and ANZ branches in Betio, Bairiki and Bikenibeu on Tarawa. Canada's travel advice says the number of ATMs is limited.

safety.text: Crime against visitors is rare and Kiribati is a calm, friendly place. The real hazards are practical: very limited medical care, thin transport links, contaminated water and, on densely populated South Tarawa, poor sanitation. King tides and coastal flooding affect low-lying areas several times a year.

tips.text: Bring enough cash for the whole stay. The UK government says very few places accept credit cards and that ATMs are found only at bank branches in Betio, Bairiki and Bikenibeu on Tarawa.

The UK government says medical facilities at the general hospital in Tarawa are modest and that any non-basic treatment usually means medical evacuation. Carry your own medicines with a copy of the prescription, and insurance that covers evacuation by air ambulance.
International flights are few, so leave buffer days before any onward international connection.
Equatorial sun on an atoll is fierce even on cloudy days, so plan for shade, high-factor sunscreen and plenty of drinking water.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Kiribati?
faq.answer: It depends on your passport. Kiribati's Entry and Visa Exemption Order 2023 waives the visa for citizens of around 120 countries and territories, including the UK, Ireland, most EU states, the US, Canada, China, Japan, Australia, New Zealand and Kiribati's Pacific neighbors; they may stay up to 90 days in any 12 months. Everyone else must obtain a visitor visa before traveling. A traveler who arrives with neither a visa nor an exemption is liable to be turned around.

faq.question: How do I get a visitor visa if my country is not exempt?
faq.answer: Apply before you travel, on Kiribati Immigration's visitor visa application form (published on the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Immigration website), and email visaofficer@mfa.gov.ki for payment details. You will need evidence of funds for the stay and of onward travel. Kiribati has very few overseas missions, so allow plenty of time before your flight.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Kiribati?
faq.answer: Kiribati's 2023 exemption order allows visa-exempt visitors up to 90 days in any 12-month period. UK travel advice says one month is normally granted on arrival and extended a month at a time by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Immigration in Bairiki, Tarawa; the order's 90 days is the legal limit. Apply before your current permission expires, since there is no other office to turn to.

faq.question: Is travel insurance required for Kiribati?
faq.answer: No official source we could read makes travel insurance a condition of entry. The UK Foreign Office advises it all the same: anything beyond basic treatment usually means medical evacuation, so make sure your policy covers evacuation by air ambulance.

faq.question: Can I use cards or ATMs in Kiribati?
faq.answer: Barely. The UK government says very few places accept credit cards, and ATMs are found at Bank of Kiribati and ANZ branches in Betio, Bairiki and Bikenibeu on Tarawa. Kiribati uses the Australian dollar, so bring cash in AUD and budget for the whole trip in advance.
